ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a four-input logic gate, with the inputs on the left labeled in order as A15, A14, A13, and A12. A15, A14, and A13 are directly connected to the logic gate, with no inversion bubbles; there is an inversion bubble before the A12 input terminal, indicating that A12 is first inverted before entering the gate. There is also an inversion bubble at the output terminal of the logic gate, and the output is labeled as CS with an overline, namely /CS, which is an active-low chip select signal. Reasoning: When the output /CS is to be selected as a low level, the internal input conditions of the gate corresponding to the NAND-type output need to all be 1. A15, A14, and A13 are direct inputs, so A15=1, A14=1, and A13=1 are required; A12 enters the gate after inversion, so the inverted A12 is required to be 1, and therefore the actual A12=0. Thus the high four address bits A15 A14 A13 A12 = 1110, corresponding to hexadecimal E. Since A11 to A0 are not decoded in the figure, these 12 bits may be any value, so the address range is from E000 to EFFF.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the labeled address inputs A15, A14, A13, A12 and note which ones have inversion bubbles. Then form the condition for the active-low output to be asserted: for the NAND output /CS to go low, A15=1, A14=1, A13=1, and the inverted A12 input must be 1, so A12=0. Thus the upper address nibble A15 A14 A13 A12 is 1110, which is hexadecimal E. Since no lower address lines are decoded, A11 through A0 are don't-cares, giving the range E000 through EFFF.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct gate-function decoding from the visible bubbles and address-line labels; this is the natural single route for this circuit.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a four-input NAND-style chip-select decoder: A15, A14, and A13 enter the gate directly; A12 has an input inversion bubble; the gate output also has a bubble and is labeled active-low CS.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the task is to determine the 8085 peripheral address range from the shown active-low chip-select logic.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use digital logic rules: an active-low chip select is asserted when /CS = 0; a NAND output is 0 only when all its effective inputs are 1; a bubbled input means that input is inverted. In an 8085 16-bit address, fixing A15..A12 fixes the hexadecimal high nibble while A11..A0 vary over 000 to FFF.
